title: Watchdog Terraform module for Private EKS control plane provisioning and staged upgrades
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Build a reusable Terraform module (watchdog) that wraps the private EKS control plane provisioning flow and provides staged upgrades + runtime health supervision. The goal is to reduce upgrade blast radius for Private deployments and provide deterministic, automated rollback when control-plane health regressions are detected. This module should be composable with the existing priv-eks bootstrap modules, expose clear knobs for canary batch sizes and health thresholds, and run idempotent preflight checks before mutating cloud resources.

Scope:
- Terraform module API (variables/outputs) that accepts existing VPC, KMS keys, and cluster configuration.
- A preflight validator step (terraform null_resource + external script) that runs: subnet/mapping checks, IAM role sanity, available AZ quotas, and expected endpoint DNS resolution.
- Staged control-plane upgrade state machine implemented via Terraform-driven orchestrator (use of SSM Parameter / step marker) to allow 1) canary upgrade of a subset of control-plane nodes 2) automated wait + health probes 3) progressive promotion or rollback.
- Health probes: kube-apiserver L7 probe (curl + client cert), kube-system component checks, and cluster-level API call smoke tests (list namespaces, create/delete small resource). Probes must be configurable and timeboxed.
- Automatic rollback: when probe failure exceeds configured threshold during canary window, module should revert to prior control-plane AMI or configuration and surface a structured failure reason.
- Observability hooks: emit events to EventBridge and create an S3 artifact bundle with logs for postmortem (terraform apply should produce a URL). Also create CloudWatch metrics for canary success/failure.
- Idempotency: all operations (preflight, upgrade markers, rollbacks) must be safe to re-run across retries and pipeline restarts.

Out of scope (for this ticket): worker node lifecycle management, on-prem air-gapped installer, and console dashboards. Those will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exists in modules/priv-eks-watchdog and builds with CI
Preflight checks run and fail fast on misconfigurations (example: missing route table)
Canary upgrade run in a test account with 2 AZs using staged rollout (canary=1/3 -> promote)
Health probes detect a simulated API server regression and trigger automated rollback in test runs
Module exposes variables for canary_batch_size, probe_timeout_seconds, rollback_threshold_pct
Logs and an S3 artifact link are produced after an upgrade attempt
Module has basic unit tests in Terratest and a smoke integration pipeline in GitHub Actions
design_notes: We chose a Terraform-first approach to keep control plane lifecycle declarative for customers who prefer IaC. The state machine for staged upgrades uses a small SSM parameter to record current stage and relies on external scripts (bootstrapper) invoked via null_resource local-exec. Trade-offs: tighter control in a controller (k8s operator) vs Terraform simplicity — opted Terraform to match existing provisioning flow and reduce new runtime components. Security: the module will require a KMS CMK ARN input for encrypting the S3 artifact bundle and IAM roles with least privilege. We scoped cross-account KMS rotation out for now to avoid complex key policies.
implementation_plan:
1) Create module scaffold + variable list (2 days)
2) Implement preflight runner and validations (3 days)
3) Implement staged upgrade markers + canary promotion logic (3 days)
4) Health probe scripts + rollback mechanics (3 days)
5) Observability hooks and artifact upload (2 days)
6) Terratest + GH Actions integration + run in test account (4 days)
7) Security review + docs + handoff (2 days)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Terraform-driven local-exec approach can lead to half-applied state if scripts fail mid-step. Mitigation: design idempotent scripts that check marker state and provide clear rollback steps; ensure pipeline runs in isolated test account before production. Risk: SSM/SSO permission gaps in customer environments. Mitigation: add preflight IAM role checks and provide a minimal policy document to attach.
